1. INTRODUCTION

1.1 PROJECT BACKGROUND

The Ministry of Roads Transport & Highways (MORTH).Government of India (GOI) has
resolved to take up the task of improving certain National Highway Corridors by the
augmentation of capacity for safe and efficient movement of traffic by upgrading to 4/6
lanes. One such set of corridors is 10,000 kms of selected National Highways under the
non-NHDP programme, spread throughout the country. The APWD has been entrusted
with the implementation of some of the development projects for these selected
stretches/corridors.

The proposed stretch from Dolabari (km 17.300 on NH 37A) to Jamugurihat (Km 182.00 on
NH 52) is a component of the SARDP-NE Project. The Project has been entrusted to the
APWD with the task of carrying out the preparation of Detailed Project Report for new
construction of 4-lane road from Dolabari (near Tezpur) to Jamugurihat on NH-52. This
report deals with proposed stretch from Dolabari (km 17.300 on NH 37A) to Jamugurihat
(Km 182.00 on NH 52) having total length of 18.810 km, including a 1200 m long bridge over
river Jia Bharali.

1.2 PROJECT DESCRIPTION

1.2.1 BROAD SCOPE OF WORK

Broad scope of work includes:

* Construction of 4 lane divided highway with 7.00m carriageway , 1.50m
paved shoulders, 1.00m Earthen shoulders on either side of 4.50m Central
verge.

* Construction of 2 nos. of major bridges , 3 nos. of minor bridges & 2 nos. of
Fly over on the proposed road.

* Construction of 40 nos. of new Box culverts are proposed including 4 nos. of
existing slab culverts are reconstructed with box culverts with same span.
* Construction of service road on both side at built up area.

* Provision of longitudinal drain at built up locations

¢ Improvement of bypass and Feeder Road Junctions,

« Sub-grade stabilization over marshy land

* Laying paving fabric beneath proposed asphaltic concrete for retarding the
Chapter | - 1
wear and tear of the top bituminous layer

« Provision of Road markings and Road furniture works

* Miscellaneous work like vetiver plantation for slope protection etc.

1.3. AUTHORITY AND PLAN PROVISION

The scheme has been included by the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways in SARDP-
NE Phase A with the aim to create a 4 - lane connectivity to Itanagar, the capital city of
Arunachal Pradesh.

1.4. HISTORY, GEOGRAPHY, CLIMATE, ETC. Assam was known during the epic period as Pragjyotisha or the place eastern
astronomy. Assam, popularly called as the land of red river and blue hills, is the gateway
to the Northeastern part of India. Assam is strategically located and has international
border with as many as four countries namely China, Myanmar, Bhutan, and
Bangladesh. It is ordered in the North & East by the kingdom of Bhutan and Arunachal
Pradesh. Along the South lies Nagaland, Manipur and Mizoram, Meghalaya lies to the
South- West, Bengal and Bangladesh to her West. It is situated between 90-96 degree East longitude and 24-28 degree North latitude. The
total area of the state is 78523.59 sq. km. It consists of 27 Districts with projected
population of 30,113,000 by 2010. Sonitpur is an administrative district of Assam. The district has an area of 5324 sq. km
and its district headquarter is located at Tezpur. Sonitpur has a significant background
of history and archeology.

The district has flourishing green valley’s surrounded by hills
of Arunachal Pradesh, with snow covered peaks of Himalaya as the northern backdrop,
lavish tea gardens and magnificent archeological ruins have all contributed to make the
district. a tourist's delight and Tezpur is considered as one of the most beautiful town of
Assam. Sonitpur District is situated in between 920 16' E to 930 43' E Longitude and 260 30' N
to 270 01' N Latitude. The Northern side of the district is bounded by the border of
Arunachal Pradesh, Southern side by River Brahmaputra, Eastern Side by Lakhimpur
District (Assam), and Western side by Darrang District (Assam). Agriculture is the predominant economic activity of the
district. engaging about 70% of the population directly or indirectly. The
agriculture is characterized by mono-cropping pattern. Other major economic
Chapter | - 2
activities are tea plantation and orange orchards.

Being located on the north of the 270 North latitude and with its unique physiographic
elements, the area experiences subtropical monsoon climate with mild winter, warm and
humid summer. The average annual rainfall ranges from 1700 mm to 2700 mm. The
main rainy months are June, July, August, and September. The annual temperature of
the area ranges from 8° C to 37° C. June, July and August are the hottest while
December and January are the coolest months.

A beautiful place on Mother Nature’s lap, located in the North-East corner of the Indian
State of Assam, the district of Sonitpur lies on north bank of the mighty river
Brahmaputra. It is bounded on the North by Siang and Papumpare District of the state
of Arunachal Pradesh and on the east by Lakhimpur District. Majuli the largest River-
island belonging to Jorhat District is on the South and Gohpur Sub-Division of Sonitpur
District is on the West. The Brahmaputra is navigable for steamers in all seasons as far
as Dibrugarh, in the rainy season as far as Sadiya; its navigable tributaries within the
district are the Subansiri, Ranganadi and Dikrong.

The exact location of the district is 26.48’ and 27.53’ Northern latitude and 93.42’ and
94.20’ east longitude (approx).

1.5 NECESSITY OF THE PROJECT

This road is very important as it is connects the districts of Sonitpur, Lakhimpur and
Dhemaji of Assam and several districts of Arunachal Pradesh with the rest of the
country. Moreover the road is connected with Itanagar, the Capital of Arunachal
Pradesh. The road is very important for improving socio economic condition of the
agriculture based and tea garden areas in the project area.

Indeed, the project can be justified not only in quantitative terms (tons transported),
but also in economic terms such as source of wealth, employment and in terms of
support given to other economic activities. Through numerous mechanisms, investments
in this project will benefit the whole society by providing access to territory and allowing
poverty alleviation to take place. Consequently, this project will create and stimulate
positive synergy and enhance social cohesion and integration by giving citizens access to

the same opportunities.

2. Upper Pleistocene Sarbhog surface.
3. Lower Holocene Howli surface.
4. Upper Holocene .... Barpeta surface.

The recent terraces on either side of the river consist of fine/medium grain

8.2 REGIONAL GEOLOGY, STRUCTURE AND TECTONIC SET UP

The regional geology, geomorphology, tectonics and seismic history of the North
Eastern Region are highly significant in context to the developmental project
activities. Northeastern region India and its’ environ is both tectonically as well as
seismically very dynamic and active. Geomorphologically the region constitute
active, unparallel relief, complex geological set up and anomalous crustal
structure which are attributed to the direct collision between Indian plate and
China/ Tibet plate in the north and Indo-Burmese sub-duction plate tectonics in
the south east.

This continent collision and sub-duction tectonics has developed juxtaposition of
three tectonic blocks viz. NE projection of Indian shield with Himalayan thrust

ChapterVIII - 1
front, Eastern syntaxis of Mishimi Block and the thrust imbricated Indo Burmese
block as well as the intervening Brahmaputra and Surma valley. The entire North
Eastern India has been divided into the following tectono-stratigraphic units.

i. | The Shillong massif and the faults bounding it.

ii. Halfong - Disang - Naga thrust and other conjugate fault systems
trending NE-SW (comprising Belt of Schuppen)

iii. Mishimi-Lohit thrust system of Mishimi Block trending NW-SE. The
complex folded, faulted and jointed meta sedimentaries of the Arunachal
Himalaya having a North Easterly orographic trend.

iv. The Brahmaputra valley surrounded by the above litho tectonic units from
south, south west, east, south east and north respectively.

v. The Barak valley sediments of Neogene - Quaternary age as trifaceted
between Shillong massif-Haflong-Disang thrust zone in the north, north
east and Naga - Chin - Arakan Yoma folded belt in the south and south

east.

The geotectonic frame work of the area around the project site constitute i) high
grade metamorphics and ii) low grade metamorphic complexes which are over
printed by Himalayan fold thrust movement, iii) poorly to un metamorphosed
litho assemblages folded during the fold thrust movement in north and north east
while in the south, iv) the cover rock sequence of for deep affected by fold thrust
movement during the terminal phase of the Himalayan orogeny.

The south eastern part of the Arunachal Pradesh (Around project site) is
represented by cover rock sequence of accretionary prism and belt of schuppen. The ultra basic/ ophilites occurring in Mishimi block in association with schistose
and crystalline limestone. Ophiolites also occur in Tsangpo suture in the north
west of Arunchal Pradesh. The diorite granodiorite complex of Mishimi block is
thrusted over the frontal metamorphics with serpentines along NW trending Lohit
thrust. The metamorphic finally over ride the neogene folded sequence of
Burmese arc by the Mishimi thrust in Noa Dihing area. The highest axial zone of
the Himalaya is mainly constituted by crystalline delimited to the south by Main
Central Thrust (MCT). The Neogene granites are common along the contact of
crystalline and Tethyan sediments.

The Himalayan belt between MCT and Main
Boundary Thrust (MBT) probably represents the tectonised northern extension of
the Indian Shield with both fresh water and marine Permo-Carboniferous
sediments and ortho quartzite-dolomite sequence. South of MBT all along the foot
hills the folded and thrusted belt of upper Tertiary molasses sediment (Siwalik)

with Gondwana and Eocene rock occur at some places. The upper Assam valley is
the major foe deep for the Himalaya and the Burmese arc, where the project site
lies.

The Meghalaya plateau and Mikir hills consisting mostly of Archean gneissic
complex and Proterozoic inter cratonic sediments of Shillong group, intruded by
upper Proterozoic granite batholith and basic igneous rocks , represents a positive
shield element. This block occupies a crucial position between Himalaya in the
north and north west and Burmese arc in the south. The Dawki fault in the
southern margin of the plateau separates it from the Sylhet Plain of Surma basin.
Cretaceous Tertiary shelf sediments occur along the southern margin of the
Plateau. The Upper Assam valley forms a fore deep.

Naga Patkai belt is comprised of thick Eocene flysch sediments, coal bearing
Barail, unconformably overlain by middle and upper Tertiary rocks comprising
sandstones, day, shale and pebble beds. The ultra basic ophiolites occur by the
Indo Burmese border. The belt of Schuppen consists of several thrust slices viz.
Haflong thrust, Disang thrust, Margherita thrust, Naga thrust, etc. are prominent
features which are mostly over thrust with some overlap.

Brahmaputra valley covers the greater parts of Assam forming alluvial plains. Geomorphologically the valley, the largest tectonic Quaternary basin in India,
evolved from a foreland depression in between the Himalayan Orogenic belt of
north and crystalline massives of Shillong plateau on south. The Brahmaputra
river runs for some 720 km from east to west in Assam along a depression due
to east-west deep seated fault system and takes sudden southerly turn into
Bangladesh along a N-S fault zone to debouch in to Gaanga. Width of the valley is
between 80 and 90 km between the hill ranges on the north and south, closed to
the river, on north the basement crystal lines are exposed in the form of
Inselberges jutting out in the alluvial plains. Beyond inselberges, the alluvial
plains abut against the Siwalik ridges of the Himalayan front. Towards east
occurrence of the inselberges extends up to 94° E Long. in Numaligarh area.

Morphostratigraphically the Quaternary Brahmaputra velley sediments are having
four successive alluvial units which apparently continue with the same slope to
about 200 m depth from the surface in the western part viz. Chapar Formation
(Fm), Sorbhog Fm, Hauli Fm and Barpeta (I & II) Fm. All these formations are
having distinct level of occurrence, characteristic degree of weathering, maturity,
texture and mineral contents (lithology). All most all formations are fluviatile
origin having varying proportion of sand, silt, clay, with basal pebble bed.

In the eastern part (around project site) the quaternary deposits of the foot hills
areas of Dibang valley and Lohit hill district has been classified in conformity with

south of Brahmaputra the quaternary units are named as Doomdooma Fm,

Dangori Fm, Saikhowa Fm and present day flood plain deposit.

8.4 TECTONIC SETTING AROUND THE SITE

The East West structural trend of the Himalaya has taken a sharp bend towards
North East - North in Siang valley, Arunachal Pradesh, The available geological
data do not indicate physical continuity of the Himalayan rock units across the
Siang fracture (Nandy, 1980) into the Mishimi Block, rather the north east
trending elements of Arunachal Himalaya with its thrust sheets abut against the
NW trending structural grain of Mishimi block. The MCT and MBT are the two
major crustal discontinuity extending west to east through Himalaya, but these
do not represent single dislocation plane. The MBT is well exposed all along the
southern margin of Arunachal Himalaya up to Siang river. Thrusting along the
MBT is a late event involving the youngest Siwalik rocks of Pliocene to Pleistocene
age.

Besides these longitudinal thrust/fault, many oblique to transverse
fault/lineaments cut across the Himalaya, some of which are regionally expensive
and transverse from fore deep to Indo - Tsangpo Suture Zone (ITZ) through
Himalaya. Few of these caused noticeable off sets on MBT & MCT in Siang fracture
zone.

The most prominent and significant tectonic feature around the project site are
apparently parallel NW trending Mishimi Thrust and Lohit Thrust. This tectonic
block over rides the NW dipping thrust packets of Himalaya and SE dipping
Burmese arc respectively. The northern boundary of this block is PoChu Fault.
The frontal Mishimi thrust in this zone show late Neogene thrusting over the
